subject: mathematics
question_text: By Mathematical Induction, show that 49ⁿ + 16n − 1 is divisible by 64 for all positive integers n.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.21 — LAQ chapter 2, question 10. Four [1 Mark] tags are printed on this page (statement, Step 1, Step 2, conclusion); the Step-3 tag is not legible on the scan, and 3 is the only value that makes the printed four sum to the chapter's 7. Publisher's claims until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them. Re-cut to the 8-mark Section-C form of the 2026-27 pattern (TGBIE model paper w.e.f. 2026-27): the extra mark goes to Step 3 — S(k+1) follows.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this by induction — how you write divisibility as an equation, and what happens in the third step.

steps.label: Write the statement
steps.margin_note: One mark. Divisibility is written as an EQUATION — equal to 64 times an integer. Without that line there is nothing to substitute later.
steps.memory_tip: Divisibility becomes = 64q with q an integer. Without that line there is nothing to substitute later.

recall.must_convey: That 'divisible by 64' is written as an equation: the expression equals 64q for some integer q.
accept: write it as forty nine to the n plus sixteen n minus one equals sixty four q where q is an integer
divisible by sixty four means it equals sixty four times some integer
set the expression equal to sixty four q with q an integer
sixty four q ki equal ga rastam q integer
reject: let s of n be the statement
it is divisible by sixty four

steps.why: You cannot do algebra with the word 'divisible'. Turning it into = 64q is what lets Step 3 substitute the assumption.
common_mistakes: Leaving the statement in words, so Step 3 has nothing to use.
Forgetting to say q is an integer, which is the whole content of divisibility.

steps.label: Check S(1)
steps.margin_note: One mark. Substitute n = 1 and show the number that comes out is a multiple of 64.

recall.must_convey: That at n = 1 the expression equals 64, which is 64 × 1 and so divisible by 64.
accept: forty nine plus sixteen minus one is sixty four which is sixty four times one
at n equals one you get exactly sixty four so it is divisible
the first case gives sixty four
n equals one ki sixty four vasthundi

steps.why: Landing on exactly 64 is a good sign the expression was copied right — the base case doubles as a check.

steps.label: Assume S(k) is true
steps.margin_note: One mark. Assume it for k, then REARRANGE to make 49ᵏ the subject — that rearranged line is what Step 3 substitutes.
steps.memory_tip: Rearrange to make 49ᵏ the SUBJECT — the rearranged line is what Step 3 uses.
lines: Step 2 — assume S(k) is true, k ∈ N

recall.must_convey: That S(k) is assumed as 49ᵏ + 16k − 1 = 64q, and rearranged to give 49ᵏ = 64q − 16k + 1.
accept: assume it for k so forty nine to the k plus sixteen k minus one is sixty four q and make forty nine to the k the subject
rearrange the assumption to get forty nine to the k equals sixty four q minus sixteen k plus one
suppose s of k holds then express the power in terms of q
k ki assume chesi forty nine power k ni subject ga rastam
reject: take it as true for k

steps.why: Step 3 will meet 49ᵏ⁺¹, which is 49 × 49ᵏ. Having 49ᵏ already written in terms of q is what makes that substitution possible.
common_mistakes: Assuming the statement for all k rather than one k.
Not rearranging, which leaves Step 3 with nothing to put in.

steps.label: Show S(k+1) follows
steps.margin_note: Four of the eight marks. Split 49ᵏ⁺¹ as 49·49ᵏ, substitute (1), and gather until 64 comes out as a factor.
steps.memory_tip: Split 49ᵏ⁺¹ as 49·49ᵏ, substitute, and collect: 16k(49 − 1) = 16k(48) leaves 64 as a factor.

recall.must_convey: That 49ᵏ⁺¹ is written as 49·49ᵏ, the assumption is substituted, and everything collects into 64(49q − 12k + 1) — a multiple of 64 because the bracket is an integer.
accept: write forty nine to the k plus one as forty nine times forty nine to the k then substitute and it comes to sixty four times forty nine q minus twelve k plus one
substitute the assumption and take sixty four out as a factor
sixteen k times forty eight is sixty four times twelve k so sixty four factors out
substitute chesi sixty four common teeste integer migulutundi
reject: I show s of k plus one
heard_as: forty nine to the k plus one

steps.why: 16k × 48 is 64 × 12k — that is the hidden 64 that makes the whole thing work. Spotting it is the point of the question.
common_mistakes: Stopping at 64(…) without saying the bracket is an integer, which is what divisibility requires.

steps.label: Conclude by P.M.I
steps.margin_note: The last mark is for naming the principle. One sentence, one mark.
steps.memory_tip: Name the principle in one sentence — it is worth a full mark.
lines: Hence, by the principle of finite

recall.must_convey: That S(1) is true and S(k) implies S(k+1), so by the principle of mathematical induction the statement holds for every natural number.
accept: since the first case is true and each case gives the next by p m i it is true for all n
hence by the principle of mathematical induction it holds for every natural number
base case plus inductive step gives it for all n in n
p m i prakaram anni n ki true

steps.why: The two proved statements are about n = 1 and about a step. Only the principle turns them into every n.
common_mistakes: Writing 'hence proved' without naming the principle.
